ce_bugs.text: Email send failures in sendAddGuestsEmails are silently swallowed with only a bare console.log, masking partial success as full success
EventManager is constructed with the actor's credentials (ctx.user) rather than the organizer's, so attendee-triggered updates may run against the wrong calendar
Client validation error flag setIsInvalidEmail(true) is never cleared after a successful retry, leaving the red warning visible during the success toast
OrganizerAddGuestsEmail subject indexes attendees[0].name without guarding for an empty attendees array, which would throw
Team admin check uses && instead of ||, requiring caller to be both admin AND owner, so plain admins are denied in addGuests.handler.ts:50-53
Any booking attendee can add arbitrary unlimited guests to someone else's booking, exposing event details and turning attendees into a distribution channel in addGuests.handler.ts:55-62
No cap on guest array size and no case-insensitive deduplication against existing attendees, enabling mass emails/calendar writes and duplicate attendee records in addGuests.handler.ts:71-101
findFirstOrThrow on booking.userId || 0 throws unhandled Prisma error (500) for bookings without a userId in addGuests.handler.ts:64-72
addGuests schema has no .max() on the guests array, allowing unbounded DB writes and email fan-out (email-bombing vector); cap the array and total attendees
Email classification comparison is case-sensitive while emails are user input, so the same guest with different casing receives the wrong email template; should be case-insensitive
isTeamAdminOrOwner in addGuests.handler.ts:66-68 uses && between isTeamAdmin and isTeamOwner so a mere admin fails both branches; likely intended ||
isTeamAdminOrOwner uses && instead of ||, so only users who are both team admin and owner pass; team admins get FORBIDDEN
uniqueGuests only dedupes against existing attendees, not within the guests array itself
Blacklist comparison is case-sensitive since guests are compared raw against lowercased blacklisted emails, allowing case-evasion (A@x.com bypasses blacklist)
Existing-attendee dedup check is case-sensitive, allowing A@x.com to evade dedup against a@x.com attendees
No email normalization (.toLowerCase()) in boundary schema or handler
sendAddGuestsEmails new-guest matching (newGuests.includes(attendee.email)) is case-sensitive, causing new guests to receive the wrong email (notification instead of full ICS invite)
EventManager is built from ctx.user's credentials instead of the booking organizer's, so updateCalendarAttendees fails or mutates the wrong account's event for attendee-triggered adds
Calendar update failure (updateCalendarAttendees throwing) leaves attendees persisted with no rollback/compensation and dedupe filter prevents retry of missing calendar update/emails
Authorization bug: isTeamAdminOrOwner uses && instead of ||, denying team admins who are not owners
Unhandled prisma.user.findFirstOrThrow with booking.userId || 0 causes raw 500 for bookings with null userId instead of proper TRPC error
Case-sensitivity gaps: guest emails not lowercased so blacklist and attendee dedupe checks can be bypassed, producing duplicate attendees
EventManager built with acting user's credentials instead of organizer's, causing calendar update failure when non-organizer adds guests
No server-side duplicate-submit protection; non-idempotent createMany allows double-tap/two-tab duplicate inserts; consider unique constraint on (bookingId, email)
isInvalidEmail error state never cleared when user edits emails, causing stale error banner and conflating server/client errors
Authorization logic uses && instead of || in isTeamAdminOrOwner, denying access to team admins/owners who aren't the booking organizer
Blacklist bypass via case sensitivity: guest emails aren't lowercased/normalized before blacklist and duplicate-attendee checks
Server-side schema doesn't dedupe the guest list, allowing duplicate attendee rows and duplicate emails when mutation is called directly
Calendar update uses the calling user's credentials instead of the booking organizer's credentials, potentially updating the wrong calendar or failing
No seat-capacity check when adding guests to seated event types, allowing guests beyond the configured limit
Blacklist guest email check is case-sensitive, allowing uppercase-variant emails to bypass the blacklist
Duplicate-attendee check is case-sensitive, allowing case-variant emails to create duplicate attendees and calendar/ics entries
Email send failures are swallowed with console.log and the handler still returns 'Guests added', so UI reports success while guests were never notified
Client clears entered emails on success even when emails failed to send, so the guest list cannot be recovered
DB write succeeds before calendar update with no transaction/rollback, so a calendar failure leaves guests persisted but mutation reports failure
Retry path is broken: re-running the handler hits empty-guests BAD_REQUEST since guests already exist, preventing re-notification
No booking status check, allowing guests to be added to CANCELLED or REJECTED bookings
ics attachment sent with status CONFIRMED and method REQUEST, re-confirming cancelled meetings in attendees' calendars
seatsPerTimeSlot capacity is never enforced, allowing unlimited guests beyond seated-event capacity
Authorization uses && so user must be both team admin AND owner, likely locking out owners
isAttendee grants add-guest rights to any attendee while the booker (booking.email) is not checked, an inverted/incomplete authorization intent
Calendar event is updated using the requesting user's credentials instead of the organizer's, causing failures or divergent state when an attendee triggers the flow
isInvalidEmail warning never resets when the user edits input, persisting until Cancel
findFirstOrThrow on booking.userId || 0 for team bookings throws an unhandled Prisma record-not-found as a raw 500 instead of a clean TRPC error

mrv_findings.text: Permission logic inverted: isTeamAdminOrOwner uses && instead of ||, so team admins get FORBIDDEN on bookings they administer (addGuests.handler.ts:47-49)

Blacklist check is case-sensitive: blacklistedGuestEmails is lowercased but guest input is compared verbatim, allowing Blocked@Spam.com to bypass blocked@spam.com, and dedupe against attendee.email is also case-sensitive (addGuests.handler.ts:66-74)

renderEmail called with 'AttendeeAddGuestsEmail'/'OrganizerAddGuestsEmail' but names never registered in renderEmail's registry, so email sends throw at render time and are silently swallowed — no emails delivered while API returns success (attendee-add-guests-email.ts:24, organizer-add-guests-email.ts:29)
Import of getUsersCredentials from '@calcom/lib/server/getUsersCredentials' references a module that does not exist in the repo, causing build/module-resolution failure (addGuests.handler.ts:6)
Icon and Tooltip imported from @calcom/ui but never used, causing lint/CI failure with no-unused-vars (AddGuestsDialog.tsx:12-19)
Authorization logic uses && instead of ||, so team admins/organizers' teammates cannot add guests and get FORBIDDEN
No booking status check: guests can be added to cancelled, rejected, or pending bookings, sending CONFIRMED requests for dead events
No tests or automated verification for the new addGuests server logic (handler, schema, email templates, sendAddGuestsEmails)
Email duplicate/blacklist comparisons are case-sensitive, allowing duplicate attendees and bypassing the blacklist with differing email casing
Seated event types not handled: adding guests does not create seat-reference records, making attendees invisible to seat capacity and notifications
eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees is called with the calling user's credentials instead of the organizer's, so calendar updates may fail for attendee-initiated adds
BookingListItem renders the additional_guests action unconditionally, including for cancelled/rejected/pending and past bookings
AddGuestsDialog isInvalidEmail error state is never reset on success or dialog reopen, so the error banner persists
Permission check at addGuests.handler.ts:59-61 uses && between isTeamAdmin and isTeamOwner, making it owner-only and blocking team admins from adding guests unlike other booking actions

Uniqueness invariant enforced only client-side; server schema lacks uniqueness/non-empty refinement and uniqueGuests filter doesn't dedupe input, allowing duplicate attendee rows via direct tRPC call (addGuests.handler.ts:70-78)
No booking state check: guests can be added to cancelled/rejected/completed bookings, sending CONFIRMED ICS REQUEST emails for cancelled events (addGuests.handler.ts:47-67)

Any existing attendee can mutate the booking and trigger calendar updates; EventManager built from ctx.user credentials (caller's) instead of organizer's, causing credential mismatch; ZAddGuestsInputSchema lacks max guests length enabling email spam (addGuests.handler.ts:55-57, 170-172)
Action id/testid 'add_members' in BookingListItem.tsx:193-200 doesn't match the guests feature, misleading future tests/analytics
isInvalidEmail in AddGuestsDialog.tsx:52-59 is set on validation failure but never cleared when user fixes emails, leaving stale error banner
sendAddGuestsEmails in email-manager.ts:538-544 emails all attendees, leaking other attendees' identities and ignoring the seatsShowAttendees privacy setting for seat-based events
addGuests.handler.ts:60-62 uses && instead of || in isTeamAdminOrOwner, making the permission check effectively false for all team members
addGuests.handler.ts:60-62 passes booking.eventType?.teamId ?? 0, invoking isTeamAdmin/isTeamOwner on a fabricated teamId when booking has no team
addGuests.handler.ts:69-71 grants attendees full mutation rights to add arbitrary guests to bookings, with no boundary between read and write access
addGuests.schema.ts has no .max() on the guests array, allowing unbounded guest lists and unlimited calendar updates/email blasts
TOCTOU race: two concurrent addGuests calls both read the same attendee set and insert duplicate attendees, with no UNIQUE(bookingId, email) constraint on Attendee to backstop
Case-sensitive attendee dedupe: incoming guest email case differs from stored attendee email, so duplicates are inserted as second rows
Case-sensitive blacklist check: lowercased blacklist doesn't match non-lowercased incoming guest, allowing blacklisted emails like Victim@x.com to bypass

addGuests.handler.ts:71+159-163 runs calendar updates using the caller's credentials via EventManager instead of the organizer's, targeting the wrong principal and silently failing for attendee callers
No status guard: guests can be added to cancelled/rejected bookings since findFirst has no status filter and update has no WHERE status guard
email-manager.ts:536-544 uses case-sensitive newGuests.includes(attendee.email), misrouting just-added guests to AttendeeAddGuestsEmail instead of AttendeeScheduledEmail
addGuests.handler.ts:168-172 swallows email send failures with console.log (without logging err) and returns success, leaving attendees persisted but unnotified with no retry or signal
addGuests.handler.ts:88-96 assigns the organizer's timeZone and locale to every new guest, making all future personalization wrong with no path to correct it
_router.tsx/handler:28 booking lookup by bare id is not tenancy-scoped, concentrating authorization correctness in a single miswritten boolean predicate
Permission check uses && instead of || for isTeamAdminOrOwner, so only users who are both admin and owner pass; admins see the UI action but get FORBIDDEN
Blacklisted or duplicate guest emails are silently filtered with no feedback while the handler still returns 'Guests added' success
Attendees can add arbitrary guests to any booking they attend, enabling email/calendar spam with no cap on guests.length
updateCalendarAttendees runs with the acting user's credentials instead of the booking organizer's, so guests may not be added to the correct calendar
Blacklist comparison is case-sensitive on the guest side, allowing 'Spam@x.com' to bypass a blacklist entry 'spam@x.com'
Guest email blacklist is bypassable by case variation: blacklist entries are lowercased but incoming guest email is compared as-is without toLowerCase()
Server-side schema drops uniqueness validation enforced client-side, allowing duplicate and case-duplicate guests to be persisted and emailed
No cap on guest array length allows a single mutation to mass-email arbitrarily many addresses
Booking lookup by user-supplied bookingId has no tenant/organizer scope, creating an existence oracle via NOT_FOUND vs FORBIDDEN responses
Any attendee (not just organizer) can add guests to a booking, enabling authorization bypass for third parties' meetings and mail-spam under organizer identity
isTeamAdminOrOwner check uses && (requiring both admin and owner) instead of ||, appearing inverted so non-owner admins are denied
Caught error in AddGuestsEmails sending is silently swallowed with no detail (no stack, bookingId), making email failures undiagnable
addGuests.handler.ts:52-54 — isTeamAdminOrOwner uses && instead of ||, denying plain team admins; likely-inverted permission logic with no test coverage (P1)

addGuests.handler.ts:74-82 — 'all guests filtered out' error branch (emails_must_be_unique_valid) untested and unreachable via UI client validation; silent-drop semantics for duplicates/blacklisted emails unguarded (P2)
email-manager.ts:525-550 — sendAddGuestsEmails two-branch attendee routing is case-sensitive; Guest@Example.com vs guest@example.com mismatch causes wrong email template for both guest types (P1)
addGuests.handler.ts:168-172 — catch block swallows errors with console.log, discarding err entirely; silently failed guest notifications invisible in prod (P2)

addGuests.handler.ts — eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees and credential resolution use caller's credentials instead of organizer's when caller is an attendee; untested non-organizer path could update wrong user's calendar (P1)
MultiEmail.tsx — new interactive component with no test covering remove/add-another/empty-state branches; splice index regression risk (P2)
Case-sensitive duplicate check at addGuests.handler.ts:66-69 (guest === attendee.email vs. lowercased blacklist) can create near-duplicate attendee rows for differently-cased emails
